why: Design 14 exploring less in bright light, where its rhythm costs beat (check 4: day beat 0.156 vs B8's 0.100; ~25% running at the mouth), and as much or more in the far field. Q's bias -3 -> -1.7: R2 flips on when Q_out falls to 0.25 (y_Q 0.6) and off when it passes 0.516 (y_Q 1.76), and at rest y_Q settles near 8 x R2's leak (~0.3-0.5), so the rest's end now lies close to where Q settles and rests stretch: ~1.4-1.9 tau in bright light, while runs shorten slightly (~0.17 tau). Dm -> Q -8: in dim light (Dm ~0.2-0.3) Q's rest target falls to ~-1.2 to -2, so rests there take ~0.4-0.5 tau, and runs ~0.27 tau. With tau 100: bright, runs ~17 ticks, rests ~144 (~11% running); far field, runs ~27, rests ~37 (~42%); between (light 0.1-0.15, Dm 0.12-0.2) rests ~50-70. A climb still holds a run (R1 -> R2 +8 against Q, which saturates as before); a fall still ends one. Everything else is design 14's. Expected in probes: steady-light running share ~10-15% from light 0.3 up and ~35-45% at 0.03-0.05; ramps > 90%, falls < 10%. In the walk calculator: crossing from 6,000 R no slower than design 14's 1.09 h. Watch-points: at night Dm is ~0.45, so the rhythm runs more at night (front nodes beat ~0.07 when it runs), adding a little night beat; the rest's end now sits near Q's resting level, so R2's leak (which sets that level) matters more in bright light.
